fullPassage: I’m Elias Walter. In my first year, I was too ①<u>shy</u> to speak up in class. I just sat quietly and never raised my hand. But my English teacher ②<u>encouraged</u> me to share my ideas. At first, it was really ③<u>comfortable</u>, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even ④<u>leading</u> group discussions. So don’t be ⑤<u>afraid</u> to leave your comfort zone.

questions.passage: Dear future students, I’m Nahyeon Kim, and I graduated last year. ① When I was in high school, I often compared myself to others and felt like I wasn’t good enough. ② I spent so much time worrying about what other people thought of me. ③ Once I stopped doing that, I began to see how much I had actually grown. ④ So my advice is: compare yourself only to yesterday-you.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Then one day, a teacher told me to stop comparing myself to others and start comparing myself to who I was yesterday."

det.korean: 남들과 비교하며 걱정하던 중, 선생님이 어제의 나와 비교하라는 조언을 해 주었고, 그 후 비교를 멈추자 성장을 깨달았다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 남과 비교하며 걱정(②) → 선생님 조언(삽입 문장) → 비교를 멈추자 성장 실감(③ 뒤)으로 자연스러운 흐름
❌ ①: 아직 비교 습관 언급 전
❌ ②: 비교 습관 설명 도중 → 이르다
❌ ④: 이미 결론 → 시간 순서 역전
det.tip: 원인(비교 습관) → 전환점(선생님 조언) → 결과(성장 실감)의 흐름을 파악

questions.passage: Hi, I’m Elias Walter. ① In my first year, I was too shy to speak up in class. I just sat quietly and never raised my hand. ② At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it. ③ By the end of high school, I was even leading group discussions. ④ So don’t be afraid to leave your comfort zone.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"But my English teacher encouraged me to share my ideas, even if they weren’t perfect."

det.korean: 수업에서 조용히 앉아만 있었는데, 선생님의 격려로 의견을 나누기 시작했고, 처음엔 무서웠지만 익숙해졌다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ②: 수줍어서 손을 안 들었음(①) → 선생님 격려(삽입 문장) → 무서웠지만 익숙해짐(② 뒤)으로 자연스러운 연결
❌ ①: 아직 수줍음 언급 전
❌ ③: 이미 익숙해진 후
❌ ④: 결론 직전 → 맥락 불일치
det.tip: 문제 상황(수줍음) → 전환점(선생님 격려) → 변화(적응)의 구조

questions.passage: I used to compare myself to others all the time, but a teacher changed my perspective. Now I believe we should __________________________________________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

yourself / only / compare / who / to / were / yesterday / you

det.korean: "compare yourself only to who you were yesterday" → 어제의 너 자신에게만 비교하라.
det.analysis:
compare(동사) + yourself(목적어) + only(부사) + to who you were yesterday(전치사구+관계절)
who you were yesterday = 어제의 네가 누구였는지
det.tip: compare A to B 구문: A=yourself, B=who you were yesterday

questions.wa: compare yourself only to who you were yesterday
accept: compare yourself only to who you were yesterday
Compare yourself only to who you were yesterday

questions.passage: Abigail Princeton advised us to spend less energy on things beyond our power. Instead, we should __________________________________________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

can / what / on / focus / control / you

det.korean: "focus on what you can control" → 네가 통제할 수 있는 것에 집중하라.
det.analysis:
focus on(동사구) + what you can control(명사절)
what = ~하는 것, 선행사 포함 관계대명사
det.tip: focus on + 명사절(what ~): ~하는 것에 집중하다

questions.wa: focus on what you can control
accept: focus on what you can control
Focus on what you can control

questions.passage: When I was in high school, I often ①<u>compared</u> myself to others and felt like I wasn’t good enough. I spent so much time ②<u>worrying</u> about what other people ③<u>thought</u> of me. Then one day, a teacher told me to stop ④<u>to compare</u> myself to others. Once I stopped doing that, I began to see how much I ⑤<u>had</u> actually grown.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to compare → comparing: stop + ~ing는 "~하는 것을 멈추다"이다. stop + to부정사는 "~하기 위해 멈추다"이므로 문맥상 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ to compare: stop ~ing(~하는 것을 멈추다) → comparing이 적절
✅ ① compared: 과거형 동사 → 올바름
✅ ② worrying: spend time ~ing → 올바름
✅ ③ thought: 과거형 동사 → 올바름
✅ ⑤ had: 과거완료(had grown) → 올바름
det.tip: stop ~ing = ~하는 것을 멈추다 / stop to V = ~하기 위해 멈추다

questions.passage: At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even __________ group discussions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: was even __________ → was leading(과거진행형). "졸업 무렵에는 심지어 그룹 토론을 이끌고 있었다."
det.analysis:
✅ ③ leading: was + ~ing = 과거진행형
❌ ① lead: 원형 → was 뒤에 부적절
❌ ② led: was led = 수동태 → 문맥상 능동
❌ ④ to be led: 수동 부정사 → 부적절
det.tip: was + ~ing = 과거진행형 (능동, 진행 중인 동작)

questions.passage: There is a big difference between your circle of concern and your circle of influence. Your circle of concern includes everything __________ worries you, but your circle of influence covers only the things you can actually change.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사가 everything이므로 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. everything, anything 등 부정대명사 뒤에는 that을 쓴다. 단, 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사이므로 that이 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: everything 뒤 관계대명사 → that (부정대명사 선행사)
❌ ② what: 선행사 포함 → everything과 중복
❌ ③ which: 부정대명사(everything) 뒤에는 that 선호
❌ ④ where: 장소 아님
det.tip: everything/anything/nothing + that: 부정대명사 뒤 관계대명사는 that

questions.passage: I’m Elias Walter. In my first year, I was too ①<u>shy</u> to speak up in class. I just sat quietly and never raised my hand. But my English teacher ②<u>encouraged</u> me to share my ideas. At first, it was really ③<u>comfortable</u>, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even ④<u>leading</u> group discussions. So don’t be ⑤<u>afraid</u> to leave your comfort zone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 "really scary"(무서운). ③ comfortable(편안한)은 scary의 반의어로 부적절. 처음 의견을 말하는 것이 편안했다는 것은 문맥과 맞지 않다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ comfortable(편안한): 원문 scary(무서운) → 처음엔 무서웠다는 문맥
✅ ① shy(수줍은): 원문 일치
✅ ② encouraged(격려했다): 원문 일치
✅ ④ leading(이끄는): 원문 일치
✅ ⑤ afraid(두려워하는): 원문 일치
det.tip: scary(무서운) ↔ comfortable(편안한) — "At first, it was really ___": 처음엔 무서웠다가 자연스러움

questions.passage: Your circle of concern includes everything that ①<u>worries</u> you—global problems, other people’s opinions, the weather. But you can’t really ②<u>control</u> those things. Your circle of influence, on the other hand, covers what you can actually ③<u>change</u>. When you ④<u>shrink</u> your circle of influence, you feel more powerful and less stressed. Focus your energy ⑤<u>wisely</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문 맥락은 영향력의 범위를 expand(넓히다)해야 한다는 것이다. ④ shrink(줄이다)는 expand의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ shrink(줄이다): 문맥상 expand(넓히다) → 영향력 범위를 넓혀야 더 강력해진다
✅ ① worries(걱정시키다): 문맥 일치
✅ ② control(통제하다): 문맥 일치
✅ ③ change(바꾸다): 문맥 일치
✅ ⑤ wisely(현명하게): 문맥 일치
det.tip: shrink(줄이다) ↔ expand(넓히다) — 영향력의 범위를 넓혀야 효과적

questions.passage: I often compared myself to others and felt like I wasn’t good enough. Then one day, a teacher told me to stop comparing myself to others and start comparing myself to __________. Once I did that, I began to see how much I had actually grown.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선생님이 남과 비교하지 말고 어제의 나 자신과 비교하라고 조언했다. 그 후 실제로 성장한 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② who you were yesterday: "어제의 너" → 본문 핵심 조언
❌ ① what others expect of you: 타인의 기대 → 본문 취지와 반대
❌ ③ the ideal version of yourself: 이상적인 나 → 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ your classmates’ grades: 성적 비교 → 본문 취지와 반대
det.tip: 핵심 메시지: 남과의 비교 대신 어제의 나와 비교하라

questions.passage: At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even leading group discussions. So don’t be afraid to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음엔 무서웠지만 점점 익숙해져서 토론도 이끌게 되었다. 따라서 안전지대를 벗어나는 것을 두려워하지 말라는 조언이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ leave your comfort zone: 안전지대를 벗어나라 → 본문 결론
❌ ① follow everyone else’s path: 남의 길을 따르라 → 무관
❌ ② avoid challenges completely: 도전을 피하라 → 반대
❌ ③ stay inside your comfort zone: 안전지대에 머물라 → 반대
det.tip: comfort zone을 떠나는 것 = 도전하는 것 → 성장의 핵심

questions.passage: Once I stopped doing that, I began to see how much I had __________ (actual) grown.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: actual(형용사) → actually(부사): 동사 grown을 수식하는 부사 필요. "실제로 성장한"
det.analysis:
actual(형용사) → actually(부사)
had actually grown: 과거분사(grown)를 수식하는 부사
actually = 실제로
det.tip: actual → actually — 형용사 → -ly 부사화

questions.passage: When you expand your circle of influence, you feel more __________ (power) and less stressed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: power(명사) → powerful(형용사): feel + 형용사(보어). "더 강력하게 느끼다"
det.analysis:
power(명사) → powerful(형용사)
feel + 형용사 = ~하게 느끼다
more powerful = 더 강력한 (비교급)
det.tip: power → powerful / hope → hopeful — 명사 → -ful 형용사화. feel 뒤에는 형용사!

questions.passage: At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even leading group discussions. So don’t be afraid to leave your comfort zone.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Elias가 두려워하지 말고 벗어나라고 조언한 것을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "don’t be afraid to leave your comfort zone" → 안전지대
det.analysis:
Elias의 조언 = leave your comfort zone
2단어 답 = comfort zone
det.tip: comfort zone = 안전지대, 편안한 영역

questions.passage: There is a big difference between your circle of concern and your circle of influence. Your circle of concern includes everything that worries you. Your circle of influence covers only the things you can actually change.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Abigail이 말한, 실제로 바꿀 수 있는 것들을 포함하는 범위를 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "your circle of influence covers only the things you can actually change" → 영향력의 범위
det.analysis:
실제로 바꿀 수 있는 범위 = circle of influence
3단어 답 = circle of influence
det.tip: circle of influence(영향력의 범위) vs circle of concern(관심의 범위)

questions.passage: I’m Elias Walter. In my first year, I was too shy to speak up in class. I just sat quietly and never raised my hand. But my English teacher encouraged me to share my ideas, even if they weren’t perfect. At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "I was too shy to speak up" + "it was really scary" → Elias는 처음에 발표가 두려웠다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Elias는 처음에 발표가 두려웠다: "too shy to speak up" + "really scary" → 일치
❌ ① Nahyeon은 자신감이 넘쳤다: "felt like I wasn’t good enough" → 반대
❌ ③ Abigail은 걱정의 범위에 집중: 영향력의 범위에 집중하라고 함
❌ ④ 같은 학교: 본문에 언급 없음
det.tip: 핵심 감정 표현 대조: shy, scary → 두려움

ch: Elias는 처음에 수업 시간에 발표하는 것이 두려웠다.
세 졸업생 모두 같은 학교를 다녔다.

questions.passage: Your circle of concern includes everything that worries you—global problems, other people’s opinions, the weather. But you can’t really control those things. Your circle of influence, on the other hand, covers what you can actually change. When you expand your circle of influence, you feel more powerful and less stressed. Focus your energy wisely.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: Abigail은 영향력의 범위(circle of influence)를 넓히라고 했지, 걱정의 범위(circle of concern)를 넓히라고 한 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 걱정의 범위를 넓히라: 원문은 "expand your circle of influence" → 영향력의 범위
✅ ① Nahyeon 선생님 조언: "a teacher told me" → 일치
✅ ② Elias 그룹 토론: "leading group discussions" → 일치
✅ ④ 세 졸업생 편지: "Letters from Recent Graduates" → 일치
det.tip: concern(걱정) vs influence(영향력): 넓혀야 할 것은 influence

ch: Elias는 고등학교 말에 그룹 토론을 이끌었다.
세 졸업생 모두 후배들에게 편지를 썼다.

questions.passage: I’m Nahyeon Kim, and I graduated last year. When I was in high school, I often compared myself to others and felt like I wasn’t good enough.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Nahyeon Kim used to compare herself to other people in high school."

det.korean: "I often compared myself to others" → Nahyeon은 고등학교 때 자주 남과 비교했다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "often compared myself to others" → 정확히 일치
det.tip: often compared myself to others = 자주 남과 비교했다

questions.passage: But my English teacher encouraged me to share my ideas, even if they weren’t perfect. At first, it was really scary, but little by little, I got used to it. By the end of high school, I was even leading group discussions.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Elias found it easy to share his ideas from the very beginning."

det.korean: 본문: "At first, it was really scary" → 처음부터 쉬웠던 것이 아니라 무서웠다. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: "really scary" ≠ "easy", "from the very beginning" → 처음엔 무서웠다
det.tip: easy(쉬운) ≠ scary(무서운) — 처음부터가 아니라 점진적으로 적응

questions.passage: Your circle of concern includes everything that worries you—global problems, other people’s opinions, the weather. But you can’t really control those things. Your circle of influence, on the other hand, covers what you can actually change.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"According to Abigail, you cannot control everything in your circle of concern."

det.korean: "you can’t really control those things" (those things = circle of concern에 포함된 것들) → 걱정의 범위에 있는 것을 통제할 수 없다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "can’t really control those things" → circle of concern의 것들은 통제 불가
det.tip: circle of concern = 통제 불가능한 영역 / circle of influence = 통제 가능한 영역
